Transcript

Altitude sickness can affect anyone who goes above about two and a half thousand metres. The first signs are usually a headache, feeling sick and sleeping badly. Climbers often believe that drinking lots of water or taking strong painkillers will solve the problem. Drinking enough is sensible, and painkillers may ease the headache, but neither of them treats the cause. Extra oxygen helps, but only for a while. If someone gets worse, for example if they become confused or can't walk in a straight line, the most important treatment is to go down, even a few hundred metres, as quickly as possible.Q5

Extra practice · PET Listening Part 4 · A doctor at a clinic below Everest

Questions 20–25. You will hear a radio interview with Dr Mai Tran, a young doctor who worked at a mountain clinic in Nepal. For each question, choose the right answer.

Audio + transcript | Questions
Played 0×

Press Show answers to see the transcript.

Transcript

PresenterGood evening, and welcome to Health Matters. My guest tonight is Dr Mai Tran, who is twenty-eight and has just come back from two months as a volunteer doctor at a small clinic on the trail to Everest Base Camp. Mai, how did you end up there?

MaiIt started with a lecture at medical school. One of our professors had worked at a mountain clinic in Nepal years ago, and she showed us photos of trekkers being treated in a stone hut at over four thousand metres. I went to see her afterwards, and she gave me the name of the organisation she'd volunteered with.Q20 Two years later, I was on a plane to Kathmandu.

PresenterWhat was the clinic like?

MaiVery basic. There were two doctors and a nurse in a stone building, with oxygen, a few medicines and one special piece of equipment that I'll come back to. Patients often walked for hours to reach us.

PresenterAnd who were your patients?

MaiLocal people, porters, and trekkers from all over the world. What surprised me was who got altitude sickness. I expected older people, but many of our worst cases were young, fit men in their twenties. They felt strong, so they climbed too fast and ignored their headaches.Q21 Being fit doesn't protect you up there.

PresenterSo how do people avoid it?

MaiBy going up slowly. Every afternoon we gave a free talk for trekkers. The main message was simple: above three thousand metres, don't sleep more than about five hundred metres higher than the night before, and spend an extra night resting for every thousand metres you climb.Q22 Some people came in looking bored, but most of them stayed for questions.

PresenterWas there a night you'll never forget?

MaiYes. A trekker was carried in after dark, confused and unable to walk in a straight line. Those are signs that the brain is affected, and that can kill. The weather was too bad for a helicopter, so we gave him oxygen and put him in a portable pressure bag, which works like taking him to a lower altitude.Q23 By morning he was talking normally, and as soon as the cloud cleared, he was flown down.

PresenterWhat was the hardest part of the job?

MaiPeople expect me to say being away from my family, but I phoned home every Sunday. And you get used to the thin air after a week or two. For me it was the cold. At night the temperature inside our room fell below zero, and I slept in my down jacket.Q24

PresenterFinally, what's your advice for listeners who are planning a trek?

MaiListen to your body, and never go higher with a headache or nausea. Wait until you feel better, and if you feel worse, go down.Q25 The mountain will still be there next year.

PresenterDr Mai Tran, thank you.

In the text: One of our professors had worked at a mountain clinic in Nepal years ago, and she showed us photos of trekkers being treated in a stone hut at over four thousand metres. I went to see her afterwards, and she gave me the name of the organisation she'd volunteered with.

22What was the main message of the afternoon talks?
Above three thousand metres, ‘don't sleep more than about five hundred metres higher than the night before, and spend an extra night resting for every thousand metres you climb.’ That means going up slowly; water and medicine are not part of the message.Clue: The main message was simple …
In the text: The main message was simple: above three thousand metres, don't sleep more than about five hundred metres higher than the night before, and spend an extra night resting for every thousand metres you climb.

Speaking

In the model answers: Point = step of the answer frame · frame language = opinion, reason, example, contrast, conclusion · unit vocabulary = words and chunks from Groups 1–4

Part 1 · Interview — 10 short questions on 3 topics, about 30 seconds per answer

0:30Answer = Point → Why → Example
Record practice — Part 1

Let's talk about famous people and life stories.

1 · Is there a famous person you'd really like to meet?

  • PointYes, …, and I'm not even a big … fan.
  • WhyI'd want to ask him how he kept going when …
  • ExampleWhen I read his life story …, for example, I found out …
Model answer

PointYes, Lionel Messi, and I'm not even a big football fan. WhyI'd want to ask him how he kept going when he was much smaller than the other boys. ExampleWhen I read his life story last year, for example, I found out he needed growth hormone injections every night as a child, and Barcelona paid for the treatment when he moved to Spain at thirteen.

2 · Do you enjoy reading about the lives of famous people?

  • PointYes, especially when …
  • WhyThat's because small details turn … into …
  • ExampleLast month, for instance, I read … and found out that …
Model answer

PointYes, especially when the story has strange little details. WhyThat's because small details turn a well-known name into a real person. ExampleLast month, for instance, I read a short life of Alexandre Yersin, the doctor who discovered the germ that causes plague, and found out that people in Nha Trang called him ‘Mr Five’, after the five stripes on his colonel's uniform.

3 · Who did you look up to when you were a child?

  • PointMy …, who's …
  • WhyI admired him because …, even …
  • ExampleWhen I was …, for instance, … That day I decided …
Model answer

PointMy uncle Hùng, who's an army doctor. WhyI admired him because people in our village came to him whenever something went wrong, even at two in the morning. ExampleWhen I was nine, for instance, the boy next door fell out of a mango tree, and my uncle set his broken arm on our kitchen table. That day I decided I wanted his job.

4 · Would you like to be famous one day?

  • PointNot really, … / Yes, I'd love to, because …
  • WhyFamous people can't … without …
  • ExampleLast year, for example, a friend of mine … The clip …, and …
Model answer

PointNot really, to be honest. WhyFamous people can't make one small mistake without thousands of strangers commenting on it. ExampleLast year, for example, a friend from my high school, who's a nursing student now, was filmed doing CPR on a man at a bus stop. The clip went viral, and for weeks strangers stopped her for selfies, which she hated.

Let's talk about space and the night sky.

5 · Do you often look at the stars at night?

  • PointOnly when …
  • WhyIn …, the … are so bright that …
  • ExampleOn a field exercise …, for example, I … and the sky was so … that …
Model answer

PointOnly when I'm away from the city. WhyIn Hà Nội the street lights are so bright that you're lucky to see more than a few stars. ExampleOn a field exercise in the mountains last spring, for example, I did night guard outside our tents, and the sky was so full of stars that I completely forgot about the cold.

6 · Did you enjoy learning about the planets at school?

  • PointYes, I loved it, mostly because of …
  • WhyShe made the solar system feel like …, not …
  • ExampleIn Year …, for instance, she told us that …, and we spent …
Model answer

PointYes, I loved it, mostly because of one teacher. WhyShe made the solar system feel like a story, not a list of names to learn. ExampleIn Year 6, for instance, she told us that Pluto had stopped being a planet in 2006, and we spent the whole lesson arguing about whether that was fair to Pluto.

7 · Do you think there's life somewhere else in the universe?

  • PointYes, I think there probably is, though …
  • WhyThe universe is so big that it'd be strange if …
  • ExampleLast year, for example, NASA said …, and those are only …
Model answer

PointYes, I think there probably is, though maybe only very small life forms. WhyThe universe is so big that it'd be strange if Earth were the only place with living things. ExampleLast year, for example, NASA said it had confirmed six thousand planets outside our solar system, and those are only the ones we've managed to discover so far.

Let's talk about messages, photos and recordings.

8 · What kind of photos do you take most often?

  • PointHonestly, mostly …, like …
  • WhyIt's faster than …, especially in …, where …
  • ExampleLast week, for example, I took …, but the only one I'll keep is …
Model answer

PointHonestly, mostly boring ones, like lecture slides. WhyIt's faster than copying everything down, especially in anatomy, where the drawings are really detailed. ExampleLast week, for example, I took about forty photos in one pharmacology lecture, but the only one I'll keep is of my roommate, fast asleep on his textbook.

9 · Do you ever write letters or cards by hand?

  • PointYes, but only …
  • WhyA handwritten card shows …, and …
  • ExampleOn …, for example, I wrote a card to … She sent me …
Model answer

PointYes, but only on special days. WhyA handwritten card shows you took your time, and you can't just copy and paste it. ExampleOn Vietnamese Women's Day, for example, I wrote a card to the head nurse from my placement to thank her for teaching me to take blood. She sent me a photo of it pinned on the ward noticeboard.

  • PointYes, I've kept a … from my …
  • WhyHe … , and it's the only … I have.
  • ExampleIt's just … Before my … exam last term, for example, I …
Model answer

PointYes, I've kept a recorded message from my grandfather. WhyHe died two years ago, and it's the only recording of his voice I have. ExampleIt's just twenty seconds of him telling me to wear a warm coat. Before my biochemistry exam last term, for example, I listened to it three times in the corridor, and it calmed me down.

Practise

Choose 2 questions from two different topics and get each answer ready in 3 steps: Point → Why → Example

Part 2 · Long turn — cue card A or B: 1 minute to plan, 2 minutes to talk

2:00Frame: Point Why How Example Result Limitation Evaluation
Record practice — Part 2

Take one card. Note a few key words for 1 minute, then speak for 2 minutes without stopping. Answer all three prompts and the last line, and add one idea of your own if time allows.

Cue card A · A nature program or documentary (bank topic 9)

  • PointThe documentary I'm going to describe is …, a … film from … I watched it on … one …, and I've recommended it …
  • WhyThe main reason is the story … It follows …, a …, and his … In …, they climbed … in …, when the old record stood at …
  • HowThe climbers filmed most of it themselves, so you're right there in …, hearing …
  • ExampleWhat I learned most from happened on … Just after …, … gave their spare … to …, then waited …
  • ResultBoth men …, and on the way down … got …, a … caused by … I'd only met it in a textbook, and suddenly I saw that …
  • LimitationAdmittedly, it's one-sided, since …, and he …, while …
  • EvaluationEven so, I liked how it turns … into … When …, I watched … again, and …
Model answer · Cue card A · ≈ 240 words for a 2-minute talk

PointThe documentary I'm going to describe is 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible, a Netflix film from 2021. I watched it on my laptop in the dormitory one wet Sunday last year, and I've recommended it ever since. WhyThe main reason is the story itself. It follows Nims Purja, a Nepali ex-Gurkha, and his small team. In 2019 they climbed all fourteen peaks over eight thousand metres in six months and six days, when the old record stood at almost eight years. HowThe climbers filmed most of it themselves, so you're right there in the storms, hearing them gasp in the thin air. ExampleWhat I learned most from happened on Kanchenjunga. Just after reaching the summit, Nims and two Sherpas gave their spare oxygen to two Indian climbers stuck near the top, then waited hours for help that never came. ResultBoth men died, and on the way down Nims got HACE, a swelling of the brain caused by altitude. I'd only met it in a textbook, and suddenly I saw that being fit doesn't protect you. LimitationAdmittedly, it's one-sided, since Nims helped produce it, and he used bottled oxygen, while Kim Chang-ho, whose record he broke, did all fourteen without oxygen. EvaluationEven so, I liked how it turns a goal everyone called impossible into small, careful steps. When he died in an avalanche on Broad Peak in July 2026, I watched the ending again, and it hit harder.

3 prompts + the card's last line · 7 steps
Look again
  • I watched it on my laptop in the dormitory one wet Sunday last year … — Where and when you saw it in a single sentence; one small detail (a wet Sunday) makes it sound true
  • It follows Nims Purja … In 2019 they climbed all fourteen peaks … when the old record stood at almost eight years — What it was about: the person, the goal and two numbers (his time and the old record) that show how hard it was
  • What I learned most from happened on Kanchenjunga … — the Example answers What you learned from it with one scene, not a list of facts from the film
  • HACE, a swelling of the brain caused by altitude — when you use a medical term, explain it in plain words straight after it; Group 2 words do the work: summit, oxygen, peak, altitude
  • Admittedly, it's one-sided … Even so, I liked how it turns a goal everyone called impossible into small, careful steps — one fair criticism, then explain why you liked it in new words, closing on a personal moment

Cue card B · A historical event in your country (bank topic 4)

  • PointThe event I'd like to describe is … in … It wasn't …, but I find it really important, because …
  • WhyIt mattered because he was the first …, and the first …, ever to …, and when he toured … afterwards, people …
  • HowIt happened on …, when … was launched from …, as part of … The people involved were …, …, and …
  • ExampleThe detail I love is … He took …, the little … that …, up into space to …
  • ResultAs a result, … became part of real space research, one of about … experiments he did in …
  • LimitationAdmittedly, it was a … rocket and programme, so some saw it as …
  • EvaluationStill, it changed what … thought was possible. He said later that …, and for cadets like us, he's proof that …
Model answer · Cue card B · ≈ 240 words for a 2-minute talk

PointThe event I'd like to describe is Phạm Tuân's flight into space in 1980. It wasn't a battle, but I find it really important, because a pilot from a poor country just out of a long war made it into orbit. WhyIt mattered because he was the first Vietnamese, and the first Asian, ever to go into space, and when he toured Vietnam with Gorbatko afterwards, people welcomed them warmly, in Vũng Tàu and elsewhere. HowIt happened on 23 July 1980, when Soyuz 37 was launched from Baikonur, in the Soviet Union, as part of the Interkosmos programme. The people involved were Phạm Tuân, a MiG-21 pilot born in Thái Bình, the Soviet commander Viktor Gorbatko, and two cosmonauts already on the Salyut 6 space station. ExampleThe detail I love is a tiny one. He took azolla, the little water fern that farmers grow in rice fields, up into space to test how it would grow there. ResultAs a result, something from Vietnamese farms became part of real space research, one of about thirty experiments he did in under eight days. LimitationAdmittedly, it was a Soviet rocket and programme, so some saw it as politics as much as science. EvaluationStill, it changed what young Vietnamese thought was possible. He said later that he'd searched for our S-shaped country through the window, and for cadets like us, he's proof that a village boy can reach space.

3 prompts + the card's last line · 7 steps
Look again
  • It wasn't a battle, but I find it really important … — say what the event was NOT, and your reason sounds stronger; the card's own words I find it important come back in the first step
  • … when he toured Vietnam with Gorbatko afterwards, people welcomed them warmly, in Vũng Tàu and elsewhere — the flight happened far away, so one clause brings the event home to your country, as the card asks
  • It happened on 23 July 1980, when Soyuz 37 was launched from Baikonur … The people involved were … — the How step covers two prompts: When and where it happened (passive was launched: the rocket matters more than who launched it) and Who were involved in it, each person with a short label
  • He took azolla, the little water fern … — one small, surprising detail is easier to remember (and to say) than a list of thirty experiments
  • He said later that he'd searched for our S-shaped country … — reported speech in the Evaluation; with his exact words you would need quotation marks and a comma (Sheet 4, Grammar 1)
Practise

Take cue card A or B (or a documentary or event you know better): plan the 7 steps, start the timer and talk for 2 minutes

Part 3 · Discussion — 10 wider questions on 4 topics, about 1 minute per answer

1:00Frame: Point Why How Example Result Limitation Evaluation
Record practice — Part 3

Part 3 moves away from your cue card to bigger questions: role models, what records and photos teach us, adventure and risk, and where science is going. Each answer should last about a minute.

Role models and famous people

1 · What kind of people do young Vietnamese people look up to today?

  • PointI'd say it's changing: … are still popular, but more young people now admire …
  • WhyThat's because the pandemic showed everyone …
  • HowThey see these people in …, so the stories …
  • ExampleIn …, for example, our academy sent … to … to work in …
  • ResultMy cousin was … then, and after seeing …, he decided to …
  • LimitationAdmittedly, that respect fades after …, and …
  • EvaluationEven so, a role model you can … beats …
Model answer

PointI'd say it's changing. Pop stars are still popular, but more young people now admire people who do useful work. WhyThat's because the pandemic showed everyone who keeps a country going in a crisis. HowThey see these people in short hospital clips online, so the stories travel fast. ExampleIn August 2021, for example, our academy sent nearly three hundred doctors and cadets to Hồ Chí Minh City to work in field hospitals. ResultMy cousin was fourteen then, and after seeing photos of exhausted cadets in protective suits, he decided to apply here. LimitationAdmittedly, that respect fades after a crisis, and pop songs still get more views. EvaluationEven so, a role model you can actually follow beats one you can only watch.

2 · Should famous people like singers and footballers try to be good role models?

  • PointYes, personally, I think they should, whether …
  • WhyChildren copy what they see, and …
  • HowIt doesn't mean being perfect, just thinking twice about …
  • ExampleMy nephew, for instance, started … after watching …
  • ResultHe was sent off …, and his coach had to explain that …
  • LimitationOn the other hand, it isn't fair to make … responsible for …
  • EvaluationSo stars should …, but … are the role models who …
Model answer

PointYes, personally, I think they should, whether they like it or not. WhyChildren copy what they see, and a famous face reaches millions of them every day. HowIt doesn't mean being perfect, just thinking twice about what you post and how you behave when you lose. ExampleMy nephew, for instance, started shouting at referees in his school matches after watching a famous player do it on TV. ResultHe was sent off twice in one month, and his coach had to explain that shouting never won anybody a game. LimitationOn the other hand, it isn't fair to make a twenty-year-old singer responsible for other people's children. EvaluationSo stars should set a decent example, but parents and teachers are the role models who count most.

3 · Can someone who lived hundreds of years ago still be a role model today?

  • PointDefinitely, as long as …
  • WhyTechnology changes, but … never goes out of date.
  • HowYou don't copy their lives, just …
  • ExampleTake …, the …-century doctor known as … He left …, studied …, and called himself ‘…’ to show …
  • ResultHe went on to write …, and he's often described as …
  • LimitationAdmittedly, we know him mostly through …, which shows …
  • EvaluationOn balance, choosing … over … is exactly the lesson …
Model answer

PointDefinitely, as long as their values still make sense. WhyTechnology changes, but caring for people who can't pay never goes out of date. HowYou don't copy their lives, just one good choice. ExampleTake Lê Hữu Trác, the eighteenth-century doctor known as Hải Thượng Lãn Ông. He left the army, studied medicine, and called himself ‘the lazy old man’ to show he'd turned his back on titles. ResultHe went on to write a medical encyclopedia in sixty-six volumes, and he's often described as the father of Vietnamese traditional medicine. LimitationAdmittedly, we know him mostly through his own writing, which shows only the side he chose. EvaluationOn balance, choosing patients over a career is exactly the lesson cadets like us need.

Learning about the past from records, photos and videos

4 · Why do some photographs become part of history?

  • PointTo my mind, one picture can …
  • WhyPeople forget … quickly, but …
  • HowThe strongest ones show … from …, so …
  • ExampleOn …, for example, the spacecraft … turned its camera back from …, and photographed … as …
  • ResultSagan called it ‘…’, and it still makes people feel …
  • LimitationThen again, without an explanation, it's just …
  • EvaluationSo a photo becomes history when …
Model answer

PointTo my mind, one picture can say something that pages of text can't. WhyPeople forget numbers quickly, but an image stays in their heads and gets passed on. HowThe strongest ones show something familiar from a new angle, so you look twice. ExampleOn 14 February 1990, for example, the spacecraft Voyager 1 turned its camera back from about six billion kilometres away, at Carl Sagan's suggestion, and photographed Earth as a dot smaller than a pixel. ResultSagan called it ‘a pale blue dot’, and it still makes people feel how small and fragile our planet is. LimitationThen again, without an explanation, it's just a dark picture with a few bands of light. EvaluationSo a photo becomes history when the right image meets the right words.

5 · Why is it important to keep personal records like diaries and letters?

  • PointIn my view, they save the voices of …, which …
  • WhyReports tell you …, but a diary tells you …
  • HowIf someone preserves them, a stranger can …
  • ExampleTake the diary of …, a young doctor killed in … An American soldier, …, was … when his interpreter said, ‘…’
  • ResultHe returned it to … in …, and within a year of being published, it had sold …
  • LimitationAdmittedly, a diary shows only …
  • EvaluationAll in all, her words teach … more about … than …
Model answer

PointIn my view, they save the voices of ordinary people, which history books leave out. WhyReports tell you what happened, but a diary tells you how it felt. HowIf someone preserves them, a stranger can meet a real person fifty years later. ExampleTake the diary of Đặng Thùy Trâm, a young doctor killed in 1970. An American soldier, Fred Whitehurst, was burning captured papers when his interpreter said, ‘Fred, don't burn this. It has fire in it already.’ ResultHe returned it to her family in 2005, and within a year of being published, it had sold over three hundred thousand copies. LimitationAdmittedly, a diary shows only one person's view. EvaluationAll in all, her words teach future military doctors more about courage than any lecture.

6 · What can doctors and scientists learn from old records?

  • PointQuite a lot, I'd say, because …
  • WhyOne case tells you little, but …
  • HowYou put the old data onto … and look for …
  • ExampleIn …, for example, during …, … marked every … on …, and most clustered around …
  • ResultThe authorities …, and his map is now seen as …
  • LimitationOf course, the outbreak was already … when …
  • EvaluationThat's why I believe every … matters. Someone may …
Model answer

PointQuite a lot, I'd say, because some patterns only show up when you look back. WhyOne case tells you little, but hundreds written down over time show where a problem starts. HowYou put the old data onto a map and look for what the cases share. ExampleIn 1854, for example, during a cholera outbreak in London, John Snow marked every death on a street map, and most clustered around one pump on Broad Street. ResultThe authorities removed the pump's handle, and his map is now seen as an early step towards modern public health. LimitationOf course, the outbreak was already slowing down when the handle came off. EvaluationThat's why I believe every ward note matters. Someone may need it in twenty years.

Model answer

HowA government could ask for proof that you've climbed another high peak, and limit permits each season. ExampleIn spring 2019, for example, Nepal gave out a record 381 permits for Everest, and in May a photo of a long queue of climbers just below the summit went round the world. ResultEleven people died on the mountain that season, and the crowds were blamed for some of those deaths. LimitationOn the other hand, permit money feeds many Sherpa families. 8 · Do young people today take fewer risks than their grandparents did?

  • WhyOur grandparents faced risks they didn't choose, like …, whereas …
  • HowToday's risks are quieter, like … or …

Model answer

PointIn some ways yes, in others no. WhyOur grandparents faced risks they didn't choose, like war and hunger, whereas we choose ours. HowToday's risks are quieter, like starting a business or posting an opinion online. ExampleMy grandmother, for example, walked through the forest for three days at sixteen to join a medical team, and she says it felt necessary, not brave. ResultThat walk led to twenty years as a nurse. When I said I was nervous before my first night shift, she just said, ‘Good. Fear means you're taking it seriously.’ LimitationIt's true that many young people avoid physical risks, partly because parents worry more. EvaluationAll in all, we're not more scared than they were. Our risks are just harder to see.

Science and the future

9 · Will trips into space ever be normal for ordinary people?

  • PointIn the long run, maybe, but …
  • WhyGetting into orbit still costs …
  • HowPrivate companies are slowly cutting the price by …, the way …
  • ExampleIn …, for example, the … crew spent … with no professional astronauts on board. One of them, …, was …

  • EvaluationOverall, though, it changed who we picture as …, and …
Model answer

PointIn the long run, maybe, but not for most people. WhyGetting into orbit still costs a fortune. HowPrivate companies are slowly cutting the price by reusing rockets, the way airlines reuse planes. ExampleIn September 2021, for example, the Inspiration4 crew spent three days in orbit with no professional astronauts on board. One of them, Hayley Arceneaux, was a physician assistant who'd survived bone cancer as a child.   • WhyOnce cells can be told to …, a new vaccine takes …
  • HowmRNA is like a recipe telling …, so …

HowmRNA is like a recipe telling our cells to make one protein, so the immune system learns to spot it. ExampleTake Katalin Karikó. Her university demoted her in 1995 after her grant applications failed, but she kept working with Drew Weissman, and in 2023 they shared the Nobel Prize. Practise

Sheet 8 / 11 · Writing · the advantages–disadvantages paragraph · 9 stages

Writing: the advantages–disadvantages paragraph, frame by frame

After the paragraph steps (Unit 11a–11b) and the opinion paragraph (11c–11d), this sheet trains one more type: a paragraph on advantages and disadvantages, frame by frame, until you can write it alone.

0 exercises checked
1 Master frames2 Topic sentence3 Advantages4 Explanation5 Example + result6 Other side7 Weigh up8 Together9 Write

Stage 1 The three master frames

GoalLearn the fixed words of the three frames (two advantages, two drawbacks, both sides weighed) and see each one filled in beside it.
Why this worksThe frame carries the structure, so attention can go to ideas and grammar; later stages take it away a piece at a time.
Recap · the advantages–disadvantages paragraph on one card · 10 slots
  1. Topic sentence · topic + side(s) + how many
  2. Point 1 · advantage / drawback 1
  3. Explanation · why / how it holds
  4. Example · a real or typical case
  5. Result · what follows from it
  6. Point 2 · point 2 / the turn
  7. Explanation · why / how it holds
  8. Example · a real or typical case
  9. Result · what follows from it
  10. Concluding sentence · sum up / weigh, nothing new
  • Before slot 1 (Unit 11a–11b, Step 2): read the question. Does it want advantages, disadvantages, or both? Does it ask which side weighs more?
  • Three frames: A = two advantages · B = two drawbacks · C = both sides, the lighter side first and the heavier side second, weighed in the last sentence.
  • The target: 140–170 words and 8–10 sentences in a single block; formal English (no contractions, no you, no questions).
Know this
  • A frame = fixed words in bold + coloured gaps for your own ideas. The fixed words do the organising; you bring the ideas.
  • Read the question first: advantages only → Frame A · disadvantages only → Frame B · both sides, or which side weighs more → Frame C.
  • Each model on the left is its frame filled in; the tabs switch the frame and its model together.
The model for the frame you have chosen · bold = frame words

Model A · 167 words · 10 sentences

What are the advantages of reading the life stories of famous doctors?

1Reading the life stories of famous doctors has two clear advantages for medical students. 2The first advantage is that these stories keep students going when training gets hard. 3This is because they show that even great doctors failed and were doubted. 4For example, in 1847 Ignaz Semmelweis cut deaths among new mothers in Vienna by making doctors wash their hands, yet many colleagues mocked him. 5As a result, a reader can see one failed exam as a normal step on a long road. 6Another advantage is that a good biography shows the human side of medicine. 7In other words, it follows a doctor into homes and difficult conversations that textbooks never cover. 8For instance, Tracy Kidder's book on Paul Farmer describes hikes of many hours through rural Haiti to see patients at home. 9Because of this, readers learn that caring for patients does not end at the hospital door. 10Overall, these life stories give future doctors both the strength to continue and a model of good care.

Model B · 166 words · 10 sentences

What are the disadvantages of climbing very high mountains as a hobby?

1Climbing very high mountains as a hobby has two serious drawbacks. 2The main drawback is that climbers can damage their own bodies for life. 3This is because the cold and thin air high on these mountains can harm the hands, the feet and the brain. 4For example, the American doctor Beck Weathers lost his right hand and part of his left hand to frostbite on Everest in 1996. 5As a result, a single climb can change the rest of a person's working life. 6Another problem is that these climbs put other people in danger. 7It is common for local guides to cross the most dangerous ice again and again for their clients. 8For instance, in April 2014 an avalanche on Everest killed sixteen Nepali guides who were carrying equipment for foreign climbers. 9This means that one person's holiday can leave other families without a father or a son. 10In short, a hobby on the planet's tallest mountains can cost climbers their health and others their lives.

Model C · 164 words · 10 sentences

What are the advantages and disadvantages of working at a clinic in a remote mountain area for a year?

1A year at a clinic in a remote mountain area has both real drawbacks and lasting benefits. 2The biggest drawback is the distance from family, friends and experienced colleagues. 3This is because the nearest town may be hours away on roads that landslides often block. 4For example, after Typhoon Yagi in September 2024, landslides cut off many mountain villages in Lào Cai for days. 5As a result, a young doctor may face serious cases with no senior colleague on hand. 6On the other hand, the clinical experience gained there is hard to match. 7The reason is that one doctor sees almost every kind of case when there are no specialists nearby. 8For instance, in one week a mountain clinic doctor might deliver a baby, treat a snake bite and stitch a farmer's badly cut hand. 9Because of this, doctors often return from such posts more confident than colleagues who stayed in city hospitals. 10On balance, the experience a remote clinic offers outweighs its difficulties.

Frame C · both sides, weighed · the lighter side first, the heavier side second. If the drawbacks weigh more, turn the words round: The biggest benefit is … On the other hand, … On balance, the drawbacks outweigh …

Stage 1a

Model C: name the job of sentences 2–9

Sentence 1 is the topic sentence and sentence 10 the concluding sentence. The model on the left switches to Model C.
2Sentence 2 =
The biggest drawback is opens the lighter side: being far from family and colleagues.
3Sentence 3 =
This is because says why the distance is a problem: long roads, landslides.
4Sentence 4 =
For example, + one named event, a month and a province.
5Sentence 5 =
As a result, says what follows for the doctor: nobody to ask.
6Sentence 6 =
On the other hand, turns to the heavier side, a benefit: experience.
7Sentence 7 =
The reason is that explains why the experience is so rich.
8Sentence 8 =
For instance, + one specific week of cases.
9Sentence 9 =
Because of this, says what that week leads to: more confident doctors.
Stage 1b

Which kind of paragraph does each topic sentence open?

The first sentence tells the reader which frame follows. Two of the six do not open an advantages–disadvantages paragraph at all.
1Wearing a smartwatch on night shifts gives junior doctors two real benefits.
→
Benefits only, and two of them: Frame A.
2Renting a room near a city-centre hospital brings two serious problems for students on a small budget.
→
Problems only, and two of them: Frame B.
3History documentaries have real strengths, but they also have clear weaknesses.
→
Both sides are named, so the body must cover both and weigh them: Frame C.
4I strongly believe that every message sent into space should include music.
→
I strongly believe that … should … takes a side on a claim: an opinion paragraph, not an advantages–disadvantages one.
5Although a mountain field exercise is exhausting, its benefits for young cadets are far greater.
→
Both sides in one sentence, and already weighed: Frame C, weighed from the start.
6There are two main reasons why so many cadets keep all their photos on their phones.
→
Two main reasons why promises causes: a cause–effect paragraph.
Stage 1c

Other frame words for the same job: which could take the place of the bold words?

Pick the frame words that do the same job. You will meet more of them in Stages 2–7.
1Model A · sentence 2 · The first advantage is that … →
Both open the first advantage. drawback changes the side; is because is a class mistake (is that).
2Model A · sentence 9 · Because of this, … →
Both introduce a result, and Thanks to this suits a good result. In spite of this means the opposite.
3Model B · sentence 6 · Another problem is that … →
Both add a second drawback. advantage mixes up the sides; On the other hand would turn to a side that Frame B does not have.
4Model B · sentence 10 · In short, … →
Both open the last sentence and sum up; the others give an example, a new point, a contrast or a reason.
5Model C · sentence 6 · On the other hand, … →
The turn needs a contrast word. In addition, Moreover and Similarly add more on the same side.
6Model C · sentence 10 · On balance, … →
Both introduce a final judgement on the two sides.

Stage 2 Topic-sentence frames

GoalOpen the paragraph with a sentence that names the topic, the side(s) and how many points.
Why this worksThe topic sentence is a promise: it tells the reader which frame follows, and a body that breaks the promise loses marks for organisation.
Topic-sentence frames
  1. topic … has two clear advantages for who ….Frame A
  2. There are two main benefits of V-ing / a noun … for who ….Frame A
  3. topic … has two serious drawbacks.Frame B
  4. topic … causes two serious problems for who ….Frame B
  5. topic … has both drawbacks … and benefits ….Frame C
  6. Although topic … has some drawbacks, its benefits are greater.Frame C, weighed at once
  • Topic + controlling idea: which side, and how many points (two, both).
  • of + V-ing or a noun: the benefits of living …, the drawbacks of space travel.
  • Sentence 1 is a promise: one side in sentence 1 means one side in the body.
  • Avoid: This paragraph will talk about … · many advantages and disadvantages · Although …, but …
Stage 2a

From notes to a topic sentence, one part at a time

Read the notes first; then pick the parts of the frame from left to right.
What are the advantages of using smartwatches to check patients' heart rates?
Notes

Frame A · topic: checking heart rates with smartwatches · who: patients with heart problems

There are + a plural noun; the notes ask for Frame A, so benefits, then of. After of, a V-ing phrase or a noun; never a bare verb, to + verb or a whole clause. .for + who: a plural group with with + the problem. everyone, everywhere is too wide to prove.

What are the advantages and disadvantages of living in a big city during university?
Notes

Frame C, weighed at once · topic: living in a big city during university · the benefits weigh more

Although + a clause (subject + verb). Despite and In spite of need a noun; However and So change the logic. A V-ing phrase is the subject of the clause; live or students live … cannot be followed by has. A V-ing subject is singular (has); some + a plural noun; the lighter side (the drawbacks) goes after Although. .A comma only (Although already links the halves); its, not it's; greater, not more greater.

Stage 2b

Which topic sentence keeps the promise of the plan?

1 · What are the disadvantages of living in a big city during university?
The writer’s plan

point 1: rent takes most of a student’s money · point 2: noise makes evening study hard

Which topic sentence keeps the promise of the plan?
B names the side of both points (drawbacks), says how many and for whom. A promises a second side the plan never gives, C names the wrong side, D is an announcement.
2 · What are the advantages and disadvantages of using smartwatches to check patients' heart rates?
The writer’s plan

lighter side: false alarms worry healthy people · the turn · heavier side: early warnings for real heart problems · weigh

Which topic sentence keeps the promise of the plan?
D names both sides and hints at the weighing. A promises advantages only, B is an opinion on another claim, C is a fact that names no side.
3 · What are the advantages of learning history from documentaries?
The writer’s plan

point 1: old film makes the past feel close · point 2: documentaries reach people who never read history books

Which topic sentence keeps the promise of the plan?
A: two benefits, the side of both points. B promises drawbacks the plan does not have, C names the wrong side, D says nothing about either side.
Stage 2c

Fix the broken topic sentence

Something in the underlined words is wrong. Pick the correction.
1Learn first aid at school brings two real benefits to teenagers.
→
A V-ing phrase can be the subject of a sentence; a bare verb cannot.
2Storing all family pictures on one phone has two serious drawback.
→
two + a plural noun: two serious drawbacks.
3Messages like the Golden Record has two clear benefits for people on Earth.
→
The subject is plural (Messages), so have; a V-ing subject would take has.
4Teenagers enjoy two main benefits of watch history documentaries.
→
of + V-ing: the benefits of watching.
5Although a year at a mountain clinic is hard, but its benefits are greater.
→
One linking word is enough: Although links the halves, so but has to go. English does not copy mặc dù … nhưng.
6Space travel has two serious advantages for science.
→
serious goes with drawbacks and problems; advantages are clear, major or important.
Your turn · main task

Your topic sentence

What are the advantages and disadvantages of space exploration?

Decide which side weighs more for you, then write your topic sentence with a frame from the card.

Two models

1Space exploration brings humanity real benefits, but it also has serious drawbacks.

2Although exploring space has clear benefits, its drawbacks are more serious.

Stage 3 Advantage frames

GoalIntroduce advantage 1 and advantage 2 with frames that show their order and their side.
Why this worksClear signposts let a reader count the points, and the correct forms (advantage of + V-ing, is that) remove the commonest class errors.
Advantage frames
  1. The first advantage is that advantage 1 ….advantage 1
  2. One major benefit of V-ing / a noun … is that advantage 1 ….advantage 1
  3. The main advantage of V-ing / a noun … is that advantage 1 ….advantage 1
  4. Another advantage is that advantage 2 ….advantage 2
  5. A further benefit is that advantage 2 ….advantage 2
  6. In addition, topic … also verb + advantage 2 ….advantage 2
  • An advantage is general: say what is good. Names, years and numbers wait for the example.
  • Advantage 2 is a different benefit, not advantage 1 in other words.
  • advantage of + V-ing · is that + a clause (never is because) · one of the advantages (plural).
Stage 3a

Choose the starter that fits the slot

The tag names the slot. Every option is a frame; the words after the … finish the sentence.
1Advantage 1What are the advantages of using smartwatches to check patients' heart rates? a watch records the heart all day, not only during a short visit to the clinic.
It opens the first advantage: The first … is that + a clause. Another needs an advantage before it; is because and One of the advantage are class mistakes.
2Advantage 2What are the advantages of sending a message like the Golden Record into space? the project brought scientists, writers and artists together to describe our world.
A second, different benefit: Another advantage (singular after another). This is because would make it an explanation.
3Advantage 1What are the advantages of studying medicine abroad for a year? students learn to manage money, time and problems on their own.
benefit of + V-ing, then is that + a clause. drawback is the wrong side; On the other hand turns to a side that is not there yet.
4Advantage 2What are the advantages of learning history from documentaries? good documentaries let viewers hear historians and witnesses explain events in their own words.
A further benefit adds the second advantage. First of all would make it the first; drawback changes the side.
5Advantage 1What are the advantages of living in a big city during university? students can find part-time work and good libraries close to their college.
advantage of + V-ing (living), one advantage + is that. Another needs a first advantage before it.
6Advantage 2What are the advantages of using smartwatches to check patients' heart rates? smartwatches can also share their readings with the patient's doctor.
In addition, + a full sentence (with also inside it). In addition to takes a noun or V-ing; Besides of does not exist; However turns to the other side.
Stage 3b

From a note to an advantage: note → frame → sentence

The notes are in Vietnamese (the Dinh Thang method). Pick the version a native writer would produce.
1 · What are the advantages of studying medicine abroad for a year?
Note → frame

lợi ích lớn nhất của việc du học là sinh viên trở nên tự lập hơn · frame: The biggest benefit of … is that …

Which version sounds like natural English?
B: benefit of + V-ing, is that + a clause, the adjective independent. A uses a bare verb and the noun independence, C uses is because, D copies the Vietnamese word order.
2 · What are the advantages of using smartwatches to check patients' heart rates?
Note → frame

một ưu điểm khác là bác sĩ có thể theo dõi tim bệnh nhân từ xa · frame: Another advantage is that …

Which version sounds like natural English?
A: theo dõi … từ xa = monitor … remotely. B and C translate word for word (from far, patient heart), D drops is that and to.
3 · What are the advantages of learning history from documentaries?
Note → frame

phim tài liệu giúp người xem dễ nhớ các sự kiện lịch sử hơn · frame: In addition, …

Which version sounds like natural English?
C: make + something + easier for + someone + to + verb. A and B follow the Vietnamese order, D needs a noun after In addition to.
Your turn · main task

One advantage

What are the advantages and disadvantages of space exploration?

Write ONE advantage of space exploration, opening with an advantage frame. (If the advantages are your lighter side, write it anyway: you will need it.)

Two models

1One major benefit of exploring space is that it teaches us how our own planet works.

2A further advantage is that space missions inspire young people to study science.

Stage 4 Explanation frames

GoalFollow each point with one sentence that says why or how it is true.
Why this worksA list of points proves nothing; the explanation is where the reasoning becomes visible.
Explanation frames
  1. This is because the cause ….why it is true
  2. The reason is that the cause ….why it is true
  3. In other words, the point, said more clearly ….what it really means
  4. It is adjective … for someone … to verb + the rest ….how hard, easy or normal
  5. This is especially true for a group … who what they do ….who it matters to most
  • Say why or how the point is true, and stay general: no names or dates yet.
  • Listing is not explaining: a new point in the next sentence leaves the first one unproved.
  • Not the point again in the same words: add the cause, the meaning or the people it matters to.
Stage 4a

Finish each explanation with the frame that fits

Check what follows the gap (a clause? a group of people? an adjective?), then decide: a cause, a meaning, or who it matters to.
1What are the disadvantages of keeping every photo of your life on your phone?
Point

A phone is a risky place to keep the only copy of a picture.

phones are easily dropped, stolen or broken.
A full clause gives the cause: This is because. Because of needs a noun; It is and especially true for do not fit the words after the gap.
2What are the advantages and disadvantages of using smartwatches to check patients' heart rates?
Point

Smartwatches can catch heart problems that a short check-up misses.

some irregular heartbeats come and go and may not happen during the visit.
The reason is that + a clause. is because of doubles the reason word and needs a noun; the others cannot start this clause or announce a result or the end.
3What are the advantages of learning history from documentaries?
Point

Documentaries make the past easy to follow.

viewers with no special knowledge can still understand what happened and why.
In other words says the point again, more clearly and in more detail. In other word is a mistake; Another advantage starts a new point.
4What are the advantages and disadvantages of studying medicine abroad for a year?
Point

Studying abroad can be lonely at first.

hard for a student far from home to make friends in a new language.
It is + adjective (hard) + for + who + to + verb. This is and There is do not fit the pattern.
5What are the disadvantages of climbing very high mountains as a hobby?
Point

Altitude sickness can affect anyone above 2,500 metres.

climbers who go up too fast without resting.
A group follows (climbers who …), so This is especially true for. Especially for alone has no verb; the others need a full clause.
Stage 4b

Listing or explaining? Choose the sentence that explains the point

The commonest weakness of this paragraph type is a list of points with no reason after any of them.
1 · What are the advantages and disadvantages of living in a big city during university?
Point

Big cities give students easy access to good libraries.

Which next sentence explains the point?
C says why the libraries help (late hours, more books). A lists a new point, B says the point again, D is a personal example.
2 · What are the advantages and disadvantages of sending a message like the Golden Record into space?
Point

The chance that another life form finds the record is very small.

Which next sentence explains the point?
B gives the cause (empty space, long journeys). A lists a new drawback, C repeats the point, D jumps to the end and changes the side.
3 · What are the advantages and disadvantages of using smartwatches to check patients' heart rates?
Point

Smartwatches sometimes give false alarms.

Which next sentence explains the point?
D explains how a false alarm happens. A lists a new drawback, B repeats the point, C is personal and off the point.

Explain it

What are the advantages and disadvantages of space exploration?

Write the explanation for your advantage from Stage 3: why or how is it true?

A model

1The reason is that Mars and Venus show scientists what can happen to a planet when its climate changes.

Stage 5 Example and result frames

GoalProve each point with one specific case, real or typical, then say what follows from it.
Why this worksA named place, year or person convinces far more than many people, and the result ties the case back to the point.
Example and result frames
  1. For example, in a year / a place …, what happened ….example
  2. For instance, a named case ….example
  3. A good example of this is a named case …, which what it shows ….example
  4. As a result, what follows ….result
  5. Because of this, what follows ….result
  6. Thanks to this, a good result ….a good result only
  7. This can lead to a noun / V-ing ….a possible result
  • Example: a real case (a place, a year, a name) or a typical case (a doctor at a mountain clinic may …); always reasonable: no invented percentages, no my uncle says.
  • Result: what follows from THAT point or example. Thanks to this is for good news only.
  • lead to + a noun or V-ing · As a result, + a full sentence · never As a result of + a clause.
Stage 5a

Choose the example that fits the frame and the point

The frame opens the sentence; pick its ending.
1 · What are the advantages and disadvantages of using smartwatches to check patients' heart rates?
Point · an advantage

A smartwatch can warn people about a heart problem before they feel ill.

Frame: For example, in … Which ending completes the frame and proves the point?
C: a year, a large real study and a result on the point. A is vague, B is true but about sales, D invents a figure.
2 · What are the advantages and disadvantages of living in a big city during university?
Point · a drawback

Rent in big cities takes a large part of a student’s budget.

Frame: For instance, … Which ending completes the frame and proves the point?
B: a real place and a reasonable price for one kind of room. A is vague, C is true but proves nothing, D is personal.
3 · What are the advantages and disadvantages of sending a message like the Golden Record into space?
Point · an advantage

The record shows how varied human life on Earth is.

Frame: A good example of this is … Which ending completes the frame and proves the point?
A names one real part of the record and shows the variety. B is vague, C names something but proves nothing, D is personal.
Stage 5b

Which result follows from the example?

The grey line is the example. Choose the sentence that says what follows from it.
1ExampleFor instance, a trekker who climbs from 3,000 to 5,000 metres in one day may wake up with a terrible headache.→
It follows from THAT example. Thanks to this cannot introduce bad news, As a result of needs a noun, In addition, climbing boots … starts a new point and For example, Everest … a new example.
2ExampleFor instance, a watch may warn a sleeping patient that the heart is beating irregularly.→
A good result of the warning, so Thanks to this. A stroke is bad news, lead to needs a noun or V-ing, and On the other hand, watches are expensive and some watches are made in Switzerland change the subject.
3ExampleFor example, in 1979 Voyager 1 photographed a volcano erupting on Io, one of Jupiter's moons.→
What the photo taught scientists. A launch in 1977 came before the photo, the volcano did not destroy Io, lead to needs a noun, and In short ends the paragraph.
4ExampleFor instance, traffic noise near a busy road in the city centre can go on until after midnight.→
lead to + noun phrases (poor sleep, lower marks). A bare verb cannot follow lead to; students sleep better is the wrong result, As a result of, is wrong grammar and the city has many parks is a new point.
Your turn · main task

Example + result

What are the advantages and disadvantages of space exploration?

Write an example for your advantage, then its result: two sentences.

A model

1For example, space probes have shown that Venus, wrapped in thick carbon dioxide, is hot enough at the surface to melt lead. As a result, scientists can use it to study how greenhouse gases heat a whole planet.

Stage 6 Drawback and turning frames

GoalIntroduce the drawbacks, and in a both-sides paragraph turn to the other side once, at the right moment.
Why this worksReaders can follow two sides only when the turn is marked and each side stays in its own half.
Drawback and turning frames
  1. The main drawback of V-ing / a noun … is that drawback 1 ….drawback 1
  2. One serious disadvantage is that drawback 1 ….drawback 1
  3. Another problem is that drawback 2 ….drawback 2 · Frame B
  4. A further drawback is that drawback 2 ….drawback 2 · Frame B
  5. On the other hand, the other side ….the turn · Frame C
  6. However, the biggest benefit / drawback … is that the heavier side ….the turn · Frame C
  • Frame B: two drawbacks and no turn. Frame C: ONE turn, between the two sides.
  • After the turn, stay on the new side: no Another advantage in the middle of the drawbacks.
  • On the other hand (with the); On the one hand only when On the other hand follows. The drawback is that + a clause.
Stage 6a

Choose the starter that keeps the sides clear

The tag names the frame and the slot. Every option is a frame; the words after the … finish the sentence.
1Frame B · drawback 1What are the disadvantages of living in a big city during university? everyday costs, from rent to bus fares, are much higher than at home.
The first drawback, with is that + a clause. advantage is the wrong side; Frame B has no turn; One of the drawback needs a plural.
2Frame B · drawback 2What are the disadvantages of living in a big city during university? noise and crowded streets make it hard to study in the evening.
A second drawback, so Another problem. Another advantage mixes up the sides, and In other hand is a class mistake.
3Frame C · the turn (one advantage given)What are the advantages and disadvantages of using smartwatches to check patients' heart rates? the watches often raise false alarms that frighten healthy people.
The paragraph moves from the advantage to a drawback: a contrast frame. In addition and Similarly stay on the same side.
4Frame C · the turn (after one drawback: the cost)What are the advantages and disadvantages of studying medicine abroad for a year? students come home with skills that last a whole career.
After the drawback (the cost, as the tag says), the turn moves to the heavier side, a benefit: However + benefit. Moreover adds instead of turning.
Stage 6b

Turn and sides: choose the correction

Watch the fixed phrases, the punctuation and the side of each point.
1Smartwatches are useful for heart patients. On other hand, their readings are not always right.
→
A fixed phrase: On the other hand, with the.
2The main disadvantage of living alone in a big city is because students can feel lonely.
→
The disadvantage is that + a clause; is because mixes two patterns.
3The first drawback is that rooms cost a lot. Another advantage is that the streets are noisy at night.
→
Noisy streets are a drawback: calling them an advantage mixes up the sides.
4A message on a spacecraft costs little compared with the mission itself, however nobody may ever read it.
→
however joining two clauses: a semicolon before it and a comma after it (or a new sentence: . However,).
5On the one hand, a remote clinic teaches a young doctor a great deal. The work is also very rewarding.
→
On the one hand promises an opposite side later; here both sentences give advantages, so a plain adding opener fits.
Your turn · main task

The turn

What are the advantages and disadvantages of space exploration?

Write the turn and the point of your heavier side: one sentence that starts with a turning frame.

Two models

1However, the biggest advantage is that satellites now help farmers, doctors and rescue teams every day.

2On the other hand, every flight with a crew puts the lives of astronauts at serious risk.

Stage 7 Concluding and weighing frames

GoalClose by summing up both points, or by saying which side weighs more: nothing new.
Why this worksThe last sentence is the one a reader remembers; in a both-sides paragraph it is also the answer to the question.
Concluding and weighing frames
  1. Overall, both points in new words ….Frames A and B
  2. In short, both points in one sentence ….Frames A and B
  3. On balance, the benefits of topic … outweigh its drawbacks ….Frame C · benefits heavier
  4. All things considered, the drawbacks of topic … are more serious than its benefits ….Frame C · drawbacks heavier
  • Sum up or weigh; never a new point, a new example or advice (… should also …).
  • Frame C: say which side weighs more; it is usually the side you gave second.
  • outweigh is a verb: the benefits outweigh the drawbacks (never are outweigh, never outweigh than).
Stage 7a

Choose the best concluding sentence

1 · What are the disadvantages of living in a big city during university?
Topic sentence · Frame B

Studying in a big city has two clear drawbacks: high rents and constant noise.

Which concluding sentence is best?
D sums up both drawbacks in new words. A adds advice, B switches sides, C says nothing.
2 · What are the advantages and disadvantages of using smartwatches to check patients' heart rates?
Topic sentence · Frame C

For heart patients, smartwatch checks bring benefits as well as drawbacks.

Which concluding sentence is best?
B weighs the two sides and names the heavier one. A breaks the verb (are outweigh), C adds a new idea, D does not weigh at all.
3 · What are the advantages of sending a message like the Golden Record into space?
Topic sentence · Frame A

The Golden Record gave the people who made it two lasting advantages.

Which concluding sentence is best?
A sums up both advantages in new words. B switches sides, C adds advice, D says nothing.
Stage 7b

Weighs, sums up one side, adds, switches or says nothing?

Six possible last sentences for one paragraph: two of them do the job.
What are the advantages and disadvantages of studying medicine abroad for a year?
Topic sentence · Frame C, the benefits weigh more

Although twelve months of training overseas is costly, what it gives a future doctor is worth far more.

1On balance, the cost of a year abroad is small next to the knowledge and confidence it brings.
→
It names both sides (cost, knowledge) and says which is heavier.
2Overall, a year abroad gives a future doctor valuable knowledge and confidence.
→
Only the good side, and no weighing: a Frame C paragraph must say which side is heavier.
3All things considered, universities should also offer more scholarships.
→
Scholarships were never part of the paragraph.
4In short, the high fees make a year abroad a bad choice for most students.
→
The topic sentence said the benefits weigh more.
5On balance, studying abroad means studying in another country.
→
True, but it weighs nothing and proves nothing.
6All things considered, the year is worth its price, even for families who must save hard to pay for it.
→
worth its price puts the benefits above the cost.
Your turn · main task

Weigh it up

What are the advantages and disadvantages of space exploration?

Write your concluding sentence: weigh the two sides, nothing new.

Two models

1Overall, what humans learn from exploring space is worth far more than the money it costs.

2All things considered, the dangers and costs of space travel matter more than its benefits today.

Stage 8 Put the frame together

GoalFill in the frame words of a whole Frame C paragraph, then put a jumbled Frame A paragraph back in order.
Why this worksSeeing all ten slots at work in two complete paragraphs is the bridge to writing one alone in Stage 9.
The frames at a glance · A and B · C = both sides, weighed
  1. … has two clear advantages for … / … has two serious drawbacks.C … has both … and … / Although … has some drawbacks, its benefits are greater.
  2. The first advantage is that … / The main drawback is that …C The biggest drawback is … (the lighter side)
  3. This is because … / The reason is that …
  4. For example, … / For example, in year …, …
  5. As a result, … / Because of this, …
  6. Another advantage is that … / Another problem is that …C On the other hand, … / However, the biggest benefit is that …
  7. In other words, … / It is + adjective + for … to …
  8. For instance, … / A good example of this is …
  9. This means that … / Thanks to this, …
  10. Overall, … / In short, …C On balance, … outweighs …
  • Ten slots in one block of text, 140–170 words.
  • Each frame word tells the reader which slot comes next.
  • Frame C: the lighter side in slots 2–5, the turn and the heavier side in slots 6–9.
Stage 8a

Fill in the frame words of a whole paragraph

A new question and a Frame C paragraph. Ten gaps, one per slot: topic sentence · drawback · explanation · example · result · the turn · explanation · example · result · weighing.
What are the advantages and disadvantages of sending a message like the Golden Record into space?

Frame C · the benefits weigh more

(1) Although + a clause opens a sentence that is weighed at once; Despite would need a noun. sending a message like the Golden Record has a clear weakness, its benefits are far greater. (2) The lighter side comes first and it is the first drawback, so not Another; singular drawback is. how unlikely it is that anyone will ever find it. (3) A full clause gives the cause; because of needs a noun. space is so empty that the spacecraft carrying it will not come near another star for some forty thousand years. (4) One specific fact (the nearest star) proves how empty space is; Such as cannot start a sentence. even the nearest star to the Sun is more than four light years away. (5) What follows from the empty space; it is bad news, so not Thanks to this. the record may travel for millions of years without a single listener. (6) The turn to the heavier side, with the; In addition and Similarly would stay on the drawback side. making the message did something useful for the people who sent it. (7) It says the benefit again, more clearly. choosing what to put on it made people ask what humans really share. (8) A specific case from the video: a small team and many months of choosing. a small team argued for most of a year over what to include. (9) A good result, so Thanks to this, + a sentence; Thanks to alone needs a noun. the record still teaches people about their own planet almost fifty years later. (10) On balance opens the weighing: the heavier side outweighs the lighter one. its value for its makers outweighs the small chance that it will ever be heard.

Stage 8b

Put the ten sentences back in order (1–10)

The frame words that open each sentence are your clues. The answer key reorders the sentences and highlights those clues.
What are the advantages of learning history from documentaries?

Frame A · two advantages

For example, Peter Jackson's They Shall Not Grow Old (2018) restored First World War film and added the recorded voices of veterans.
Example of advantage 1: one named film and a year.
For instance, about 40 million Americans watched Ken Burns's series The Civil War when it was first shown in 1990.
Example of advantage 2: one named series, a year and a number.
Learning history from documentaries has two clear advantages over learning from books alone.
Topic sentence: the topic + two clear advantages, so it opens a Frame A paragraph.
Another advantage is that documentaries reach people who would never open a history book.
Advantage 2: Another opens the second point.
In short, documentaries make history both more vivid and more widely known.
Concluding sentence: both advantages (vivid, widely known) in new words.
This is because viewers can see the faces and hear the words of people who lived through the events.
Explanation of advantage 1: why film makes the past feel close.
The reason is that a good series turns a subject many find dull into an evening's entertainment.
Explanation of advantage 2: why it reaches so many people.
One major advantage is that real film and real voices make the past feel close.
Advantage 1: One major advantage opens the first point.
As a result, a war from over a century ago feels like a story about real young men.
Result of the example: what the film does to viewers.
Because of this, millions of families began to talk about a war that had ended 125 years earlier.
Result of the example: this = the huge audience.

Stage 9 Write it with the frame

GoalWrite three paragraphs, one per frame, with less help each time: guided frame, starters only, then free and timed.
Why this worksHelp that is withdrawn in steps (gradual release) ends in independent writing, and at Level 1 even the weakest writer finishes a correct paragraph.
Know this
  • Level 1 · Guided frame (Frame A, studying medicine abroad): each box starts with its frame. Clicking an idea fills the next gap (…); typing your own words works too.
  • Level 2 · Starters only (Frame B, every photo on one phone): the grey starter is a hint; the notes are ideas, and you write the sentences.
  • Level 3 · Free and timed (Frame C, the main task): choose the side that weighs more, then write; 20 minutes.
  • Everything you write appears in Your paragraph, coloured slot by slot; Send to the writing box copies it into Stage 9d for the Self-check.
Stage 9a

Level 1 · Guided frame: Frame A, every box starts with its frame

Each idea you click drops into the next … of its box; you can also type. With the ideas alone the paragraph has 145–156 words; afterwards, change a few words to make it yours. Stuck on a box? Press Show a model under it.
What are the advantages of studying medicine abroad for a year?
1Topic sentence·topic + side(s) + how many
topic … offers who … two important benefits.
Topic
Who

A year of medical study in another country offers future doctors two important benefits.

2Point 1·advantage / drawback 1
The first benefit is that benefit 1 ….
Ideas

The first benefit is that students quickly gain the English they need for medical work.

3Explanation·why / how it holds
This is because why it is true ….
Ideas

This is because lectures, ward rounds and everyday life all happen in English.

4Example·a real or typical case
For example, a typical case ….
Ideas

For example, a Vietnamese student on an exchange in Australia must take patient histories in English from the first week.

5Result·what follows from it
As a result, what follows ….
Ideas

As a result, these students can later follow new research and speak up at international conferences.

6Point 2·point 2 / the turn
Another benefit is that benefit 2 ….
Ideas

Another benefit is that students see how hospitals in another country organise their care.

7Explanation·why / how it holds
In other words, the point, said more clearly ….
Ideas

In other words, they discover that there is more than one good way to treat patients.

8Example·a real or typical case
For instance, a typical case ….
Ideas

For instance, a student on placement in Singapore can watch doctors share electronic patient records between different hospitals.

9Result·what follows from it
Because of this, what follows ….
Ideas

Because of this, they return home with practical ideas for their own wards.

10Concluding sentence·sum up / weigh, nothing new
Overall, both benefits in new words ….
Ideas

Overall, time abroad sharpens both the language and the medical thinking of a young doctor.

Stage 9b

Level 2 · Starters only: Frame B, two drawbacks

The grey starter in each box is a hint, and the notes under it are ideas, not sentences. Open a model only to compare.
What are the disadvantages of keeping every photo of your life on your phone?
1Topic sentence·topic + side(s) + how many
  • Frame B: two drawbacks
  • the topic: every photo only on a phone

Keeping every photo of a lifetime only on a phone causes two serious problems.

2Point 1·advantage / drawback 1
  • lost, stolen or broken phone → no photos

One serious disadvantage is that the pictures can vanish in a moment.

3Explanation·why / how it holds
  • small, fragile, easy to lose
  • no backup copy

This is because a small, fragile device is easy to lose, and many owners never make a backup copy.

4Example·a real or typical case
  • a cadet · a field exercise
  • phone in a stream → four years of photos gone

For example, a cadet whose phone falls into a stream on a field exercise can lose four years of memories at once.

5Result·what follows from it
  • moments that cannot be repeated

As a result, moments that can never happen again are gone for good.

6Point 2·point 2 / the turn
  • privacy

A further drawback is that private pictures do not always stay private.

7Explanation·why / how it holds
  • apps, cloud services, hackers
  • images meant to stay personal

It is surprisingly easy for apps, cloud services or hackers to reach images that were meant to stay personal.

8Example·a real or typical case
  • 2014 · famous people
  • online storage hacked → photos posted

For instance, in 2014 hackers stole private photos of many famous people from their online storage accounts and posted them online.

9Result·what follows from it
  • lose control of photos
  • family · home · patients

This means that a phone owner can lose control of pictures of their family, their home or even their patients.

10Concluding sentence·sum up / weigh, nothing new
  • fragile + unsafe
  • new words

In short, a single phone is a fragile and unsafe home for a lifetime of pictures.

Main task · one advantages–disadvantages paragraphWhat are the advantages and disadvantages of space exploration? Write one paragraph (140–170 words) that covers both sides and says which side weighs more.

Send your Level 3 boxes here, or write straight into the box: ten slots in one block of text.

Word count: 0 / 140–170 words · 8–10 sentences in one block · 20 minutes

Model paragraph · Frame C, the benefits weigh more · 152 words · 10 sentences

Topic sentenceAdvantage / drawbackExplanationExampleResultConcluding sentence

Although space exploration has some serious drawbacks, its benefits for life on Earth are far greater. The main drawback is the enormous cost. This is because rockets, spacecraft and telescopes take thousands of experts many years to design and build. For example, the James Webb Space Telescope, launched in December 2021, cost about ten billion US dollars. As a result, critics argue that the same money could build hospitals or buy vaccines for millions of people. On the other hand, space research brings practical benefits to ordinary people. In other words, tools first designed for spacecraft often end up in homes, farms and hospitals. For instance, the ear thermometers used on children's wards grew out of infrared technology that measured the heat of distant stars. Because of this, money spent on space can return to Earth as better medical care. On balance, the practical gains from space exploration outweigh its high price.

Now compare
  • Which frame words open each of the ten slots in the model?
  • Which side comes second, and how does the last sentence follow from it?
  • Find the turn: which four words move the paragraph to the other side?
  • Take two things from the model into your own paragraph and revise the draft on the left.
Stage 9e

From band 5 to band 7: upgrade the paragraph part by part

A student's paragraph on another question. The band scale is the IELTS-style one from the handbook; on our rubric, band 7 means scoring 3 on most criteria. Pick the band-7 version of each part.
Band-5 paragraphWhat are the advantages and disadvantages of using smartwatches to check patients' heart rates?

Smartwatch is very good for patient. It have advantage and disadvantage. Firstly it check heart. Secondly it is modern. Thirdly it is cheap. But sometime it is wrong. So smartwatch is good and bad.

1 · Which topic sentence could replace the first two sentences?
D names the topic and both sides, with correct grammar. A keeps the errors, B is an announcement, C says nothing.
2 · Which sentence turns Firstly it check heart into an explained point?
A gives the point and its reason (so …). B keeps the errors and adds a comma splice, C uses you, D is still a list.
3 · Which example could support the point in question 2?
C shows the all-day checking in one real situation. A is personal, B is vague, D invents a figure.
4 · Which last sentence upgrades So smartwatch is good and bad?
B weighs the two sides and names the heavier one. A does not weigh, C adds a new idea, D adds a new point at the very end.
From band 5 to band 7, the changes: a topic sentence that names both sides · the Firstly, Secondly, Thirdly list became one explained point with a real example · But sometime it is wrong became a turn to the other side · the last sentence weighs the sides · is/have, advantage, sometime corrected. (A full band-7 paragraph would also explain and illustrate the drawback.)
Stage 9f

Which peer comment helps most?

1 · Feedback on a big problem in the band-5 paragraph (content or organisation): which comment would help most?
C gives a strength, the problem, the reason it matters and a fix; A and B are too vague, and D picks a minor point.
2 · Feedback on a small problem (language): which comment helps most?
B names one error, says why it is wrong and shows the correction; the rest give the writer nothing to act on.

Read each description and choose the word or phrase it explains

=

Exercise 7 · Punctuation in direct speech — the correctly punctuated sentence

Exercise 7

The card shows the words with no punctuation: choose the line that punctuates them correctly as direct speech

Rules: SB p. 137 Ex 3b · Mai Lan Hương p. 317: direct speech repeats the speaker's exact words inside quotation marks, after a comma or a colon, and the reporting clause can also follow the words.
1you will feel a small scratch said the nurse
quote first → a comma inside the closing mark, then said the nurse and a full stop at the very end
2my professor always tells us read the patient before you read the chart
reporting clause first → comma, opening mark, capital letter; the quote ends the sentence, so the full stop goes inside
3is this your first night shift asked the senior doctor
the ? belongs to the quote, so it goes inside and replaces the comma; asked stays small
4stop the bleeding first shouted the instructor
! inside the mark, no comma after it, small shouted, a full stop at the end of the whole sentence
5it was a long climb said Hoa but the view was worth it
one sentence split in two → comma before and after said Hoa, small but, full stop inside at the end
6the river was too deep said the guide we had to turn back
two separate sentences → a full stop after said the guide and a capital We
7yes doctor I took the tablets said the patient
commas inside the quote too (Yes, doctor,), as in SB Ex 3c ‘Yes, we can,’
8I've never seen so many stars he said
comma inside, small he, and the apostrophe in I’ve; both marks are needed
9our lecturer said my first patient told me don't be nervous doctor
a quote inside a quote: single marks outside, double marks inside (British style); each quote has its comma and capital
10do you know asked my grandmother what your great-grandfather did in the war
one question cut in two: comma, comma, small what, and the ? only at the end, inside the mark

6The last time I saw my old teacher was in 2019.→ I my old teacher since 2019.
the last time … was in = haven’t + past participle + since
7It’s the first time I’ve climbed a mountain.→ I a mountain before.
the first time = have never + past participle + before
8Flashcard apps are useful because you can practise anywhere.→ One .
One advantage of + noun is that + clause (never is because)
9Diving without an air tank is very dangerous. That is its biggest problem.→ The biggest drawback .
drawback of + ‑ing … is that + clause · extremely (adverb) + adjective
10Learning first aid from online videos has some advantages, but its disadvantages are greater.→ On balance, .
the bigger side outweighs the smaller one; plural subject → outweigh
